name: Cape Verde
snapshot: An Atlantic island democracy with a long record of peaceful handovers; in May 2026 voters swapped governments again, bringing the PAICV back to power.
culture: Cabo Verde's islands were uninhabited until the Portuguese settled them in the 15th century, and Kriolu, a Portuguese-based creole, grew out of the mix of settlers and enslaved West Africans. Morna, the melancholy song style made famous by Cesária Évora, the "barefoot diva", is on UNESCO's heritage list. Funaná and batuque are the faster, danced counterparts, once suppressed by the colonial authorities.
society: More Cabo Verdeans live abroad, in the US, Portugal and elsewhere in Europe, than at home, and their remittances are vital. Tourism to Sal and Boa Vista beaches is the largest industry. Recurrent droughts and the lack of fresh water have shaped history, including deadly famines. The country scores well above the African average on press freedom and governance.
baseline: Cabo Verde has alternated power peacefully between its two main parties since 1991. Ulisses Correia e Silva of the centre-right MpD governed from 2016, while President José Maria Neves comes from the PAICV, the party of independence. In the 17 May 2026 legislative election the PAICV won 37 of 72 seats, and its leader, Francisco Carvalho, a former mayor of the capital, Praia, became prime minister.
